reconcile.note: The Geneva Bible annotators number the Michmash rout's own sequence of blows, so "first slaughter" in 14:14 marks that engagement's opening, not Jonathan's first combat ever.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain sense of 1 Samuel 14:14's "first slaughter" against the earlier Geba garrison killing already told in 13:3.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba
sides.verseText: Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba: and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear.

sides.snippet: That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men
sides.verseText: That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow's length in an acre of land.
